title: Amendments to two employment laws will strengthen family support from 2027
text:
At the Cabinet’s weekly meeting Thursday, Premier Cho Jung-tai received a briefing from the Ministry of Labor (MOL) and the Directorate-General of Personnel Administration on new measures to be implemented following the Legislative Yuan’s passage of amendments to the Gender Equality in Employment Act and the Employment Insurance Act. The premier said the amendments mark a huge step forward for the government’s new population strategy, particularly in efforts to strengthen family support.

The premier noted that maternity leave will be extended from eight weeks to 14 weeks, the first major increase to the number of maternity leave days in more than 40 years. Paternity leave and leave to accompany a spouse to prenatal appointments will also rise from a combined seven days to a combined 14 days. In addition, eligibility for unpaid parental leave and child care leave will be extended to parents of children under age nine, up from the current age limit of children under three. Employees will be able to take child care leave in single-day increments for up to 60 days, double the previous limit of 30 days, within the overall entitlement of up to two years of unpaid parental leave. Eligibility for unpaid parental leave with allowance will also be eased, granting each parent an additional three months of allowance if both parents have received the allowance for six months.

Premier Cho highlighted that the government is committed not only to supporting working parents but also to helping businesses, with the changes making subsidies available to cover employers' additional wage costs resulting from the expansion of pregnancy- and childbirth-related leave entitlements, while also offering tax incentives for businesses.

Alongside the amendments, the MOL is also rolling out incentive and subsidy plans to promote reduced working hours for employees with children under 12. The premier directed the MOL to swiftly finalize the relevant subsidiary regulations and supporting measures to ensure that the new policies take effect on January 1, 2027.
